ZENSAR TECHNOLOGIES

AN RPG ENTERPRISES COMPANY

Zensar Intern Knowledge

Consolidated Knowledge Base & Operational Governance Manual

Table of Contents

This Table of Contents provides a complete three-column index of all chapters and detailed subtopics. Serial numbering reflects the hierarchical knowledge structure, and page numbers denote the exact starting page of each section.

Chapter 1: Internship Overview

1.1  Internship Program Introduction

The Zensar Internship Program, operated in alignment with the Zensar Fresher Engineers Hiring Program, is an enterprise early-career talent development initiative designed to transition top-tier academic engineering talent into high-performing digital technology professionals. Structured under the aegis of RPG Enterprises and Zensar's human capital leadership, the program provides pre-final and final-year engineering students with immersive industry exposure to modern software engineering, enterprise cloud platforms, data engineering, and artificial intelligence.

Interns are integrated into Zensar's core engineering philosophy—Experience-Led Everything (ELE)—which harmonizes human-centered design with robust enterprise architecture. Rather than working on simulated or theoretical exercises, interns are embedded directly into active project environments, client-facing delivery teams, and cutting-edge innovation pods.

The program serves as the primary strategic pipeline for identifying, grooming, and onboarding future full-time Graduate Trainee Engineers (GTEs) and Associate Software Engineers across Zensar's global delivery centers.

1.2  Internship Objectives

The Zensar Internship Program is designed around five core strategic and educational objectives that bridge academic computer science theory with industrial software development rigor. These objectives ensure that every intern acquires measurable engineering capabilities, professional acumen, and corporate readiness.

First, the program builds deep competency in contemporary enterprise technology stacks, including cloud-native microservices, containerization, full-stack frameworks, modern DevOps pipelines, and generative artificial intelligence. Second, it exposes interns to agile development methodologies (Scrum/Kanban), test-driven development (TDD), continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD), and enterprise security compliance.

Third, the program instills the foundational values of RPG Enterprises—codified in the 'Values in Motion' framework—emphasizing client centricity, velocity, passion to outperform, collaboration, and ethical integrity. Fourth, interns develop professional soft skills, including structured stakeholder communication, technical presentation, and collaborative problem-solving. Finally, the program provides a transparent evaluation framework for permanent employment conversion.

1.3  Internship Duration

The standard duration of the Zensar Internship Program ranges between 3 months and 6 months, determined by the specific hiring track, university curriculum requirements, and business unit staffing models. The most common format is a 6-month continuous semester internship running from January to June for final-year engineering graduates.

During this operational tenure, interns commit to full-time corporate hours (45 hours per week, Monday through Friday). The duration is structured into distinct, sequential milestones ensuring continuous progression from foundational learning to independent project execution.

Any extension or adjustment to the approved internship duration requires formal approval from the Delivery Unit Head, the Campus Talent Acquisition Team, and the intern's academic institution (via an updated No Objection Certificate).

1.4  Internship Structure

The Zensar Internship Program is architected into four progressive phases: Foundation Enablement, Hands-On Technology Immersion, Project Shadowing & Execution, and Capstone Defense & Transition. This phased model guarantees that interns receive structured scaffolding before being entrusted with independent technical deliverables.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1 to 4) focuses on organizational induction, corporate culture, core engineering principles, version control, and coding standards. Phase 2 (Weeks 5 to 10) delivers track-specific deep dives into modern full-stack, cloud, or data platforms, complemented by daily hands-on lab assignments and weekly benchmark quizzes.

Phase 3 (Weeks 11 to 20) embeds interns into active project teams where they shadow senior engineers, participate in daily standups, and resolve real-world user stories. Phase 4 (Weeks 21 to 24) culminates in an independent or paired Capstone Project, formal project defense before an expert panel, and exit/PPO evaluation.

1.5  Internship Expectations

Zensar expects all interns to conduct themselves with the same degree of professionalism, accountability, and ethical integrity demanded of permanent associates. Interns represent Zensar and RPG Enterprises in all interactions, requiring strict adherence to corporate standards and information security protocols.

From a technical perspective, interns are expected to demonstrate intellectual curiosity, self-directed learning, proactive inquiry, and a strong commitment to code quality. Timely completion of training assignments, prompt timesheet submission, and active participation in team standups are mandatory non-negotiable requirements.

Unethical practices, including code plagiarism, unauthorized access to restricted environments, misrepresentation of attendance, or sharing confidential company or client data, constitute gross misconduct and will result in immediate termination of the internship.

Chapter 2: Internship Onboarding

2.1  Offer Acceptance

The onboarding journey initiates with the formal issuance of the Zensar Internship Offer Letter via the official Campus Talent Acquisition portal or designated corporate email. The offer letter articulates the key terms of engagement, including internship role, start date, duration, monthly stipend amount, reporting location, and applicable conditions.

Selected candidates must review all terms, execute their formal acceptance via the candidate portal within the specified deadline (typically 3 to 5 business days), and upload signed copies. Failure to accept within the stipulated timeframe may lead to offer forfeiture.

Upon receipt of acceptance, the candidate is granted access to the pre-onboarding portal to initiate document submission and background verification clearance.

2.2  Pre-Joining Formalities

Prior to the Day 1 reporting date, candidates must complete mandatory pre-joining formalities. These include submitting educational records, completing identity verification forms, and establishing a valid sole-account savings bank account for stipend processing.

Candidates receive an official onboarding welcome communication outlining pre-joining briefing sessions, virtual webinars, technical prerequisites (e.g. baseline software installation guidelines), and travel/accommodation logistics where physical relocation is involved.

Candidates are advised to stay in continuous communication with the Campus HR Coordinator and monitor their registered email address for critical onboarding updates.

2.3  Document Submission

Interns are required to upload digital, legible copies of all mandatory credentials to the Zensar Pre-Onboarding Portal at least 10 working days prior to joining. Original physical documents must be brought on Day 1 for physical verification.

The mandatory documentation package includes: 10th and 12th Standard mark sheets and passing certificates; semester-wise mark sheets of undergraduate engineering degree (B.Tech/B.E./MCA) showing cumulative CGPA/percentage; college Bonafide Certificate; College No Objection Certificate (NOC) signed by the Dean or Principal; Permanent Account Number (PAN) card; Aadhaar Card; and 4 passport-size photographs.

Incomplete documentation or discrepancies between submitted copies and original credentials will delay laptop provisioning and stipend processing.

2.4  Background Verification, if applicable

Zensar maintains rigorous background verification (BGV) protocols conducted through authorized third-party investigation agencies. All intern candidates are subjected to formal credential vetting to safeguard organizational and client security.

The BGV scope for interns typically covers: academic authenticity verification with university registrars; identity verification against national databases (UIDAI for Aadhaar and Income Tax Department for PAN); permanent and current residential address physical/digital verification; and criminal record database checks.

Any intentional misrepresentation, forged academic certificates, or concealed disciplinary actions will result in immediate termination of the internship and blacklisting from future RPG Group employment.

2.5  Joining Instructions

Detailed joining instructions are transmitted to all confirmed interns five business days prior to the reporting date. The instructions provide explicit guidance on reporting time, venue address, dress code, security protocols, and Day 1 schedule.

For physical onboarding, interns must report to the Reception at Zensar Knowledge Park, Kharadi, Pune (or the designated regional office) by 9:00 AM IST. Interns must carry their original offer letter, government photo ID, original academic documents, and 4 passport photographs.

For virtual onboarding, interns receive Microsoft Teams login credentials, calendar invitations for the corporate orientation stream, and instructions for secure home delivery and activation of company-issued IT assets.

2.6  Onboarding Checklist

To ensure a seamless transition into Zensar, interns must systematically complete the Onboarding Checklist covering all pre-joining, Day 1, and First-Week milestones.

The checklist encompasses administrative, technical, and compliance actions required before an intern is declared fully operational. Completing all items within the first 5 business days prevents administrative holds on stipend disbursement and development tool access.

Day One IT Initialization Protocol: Immediately upon receiving system credentials from the Campus Recruitment / Joining Operations team, interns must follow a strict sequential IT setup protocol: (1) First Login on ADSelfService: Access https://adselfservice.zensar.com before attempting to log into any other platform. Change your temporary password, which will remain active for 42 calendar days; (2) Mobile Number Registration: Register your personal mobile number formatted with the country code without plus signs or spaces (e.g., 919890989099 for India); (3) Personal Email Registration: Register a personal email account to ensure OTP receipt if your password expires or account is locked; and (4) Laptop Browser Webmail First Login: The initial login to corporate email (https://email.zensar.com or https://outlook.office365.com) MUST be executed through the corporate laptop browser, not from a mobile phone.

Mobile MFA & Intune Configuration: Once webmail is accessible on the laptop, configure Microsoft Authenticator Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) on your personal smartphone via https://aka.ms/mfasetup. Following MFA pairing, enroll your mobile phone into the Microsoft Intune Company Portal using your Zensar email ID to enable secure access to Microsoft Teams and Outlook.

Chapter 3: First-Day and First-Week Guidance

3.1  Reporting Instructions

On Day 1, all incoming interns reporting to the physical campus must arrive at the main security gate of Zensar Knowledge Park, Kharadi, Pune (or their assigned regional campus) at exactly 9:00 AM IST. Visitors and new joiners must present a government-issued photo ID (Aadhaar or PAN) and the electronic or printed Zensar Internship Offer Letter to obtain entry clearance.

Security personnel issue a temporary visitor/onboarding badge. Interns are directed to the designated Onboarding Auditorium or HR Training Hall. Business formal or smart casual attire is required throughout the first week.

Interns joining remotely must log into the designated Microsoft Teams onboarding room 15 minutes before the scheduled start time, ensuring a stable internet connection, functioning webcam, and quiet professional environment.

3.2  Joining Schedule

The Day 1 joining schedule is meticulously structured to balance administrative formalities with organizational orientation and technical setup. The day is divided into structured morning and afternoon sessions.

The morning session (9:00 AM – 1:00 PM) covers registration, document verification, welcome addresses by Campus Talent Acquisition leaders, and an introduction to the RPG Group ethos. A sponsored welcome lunch is provided at the campus cafeteria.

The afternoon session (2:00 PM – 6:00 PM) is dedicated to IT asset distribution, laptop provisioning, corporate network credential configuration, security briefing, and meeting the assigned buddy.

3.3  Induction Process

The Zensar Induction Process extends across the first three days of the internship, providing an in-depth orientation into corporate governance, operating frameworks, and statutory compliance. Facilitated by HR leaders and senior technical architects, the induction program establishes clear expectations regarding workplace ethics, business standards, and information security.

Mandatory induction topics include: Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) statutory training; Information Security & Data Privacy (ISMS ISO 27001); Intellectual Property & Client Confidentiality; Clean Desk & Clean Screen Policy; and Code of Conduct & Ethics.

Interns must complete digital e-learning comprehension quizzes for POSH and Information Security within 7 days of joining. A minimum score of 80% is required to achieve certification.

Structured Intern Onboarding Journey: Zensar provides a structured onboarding trajectory across the first 30 days: (a) Day 1: Welcome briefing, document submission, physical laptop receipt from TIMS counter, network credential activation, and ADSelfService enrollment; (b) Days 2–5: Corporate culture induction, RPG Group Values overview, introduction to technical mentors, onboarding buddy assignment, and ZenFusion bank details registration; (c) Days 6–15: Foundation technical training tracks, syllabus deep-dive, development environment setup via Software Center; and (d) Day 30: First formal milestone checkpoint with technical mentors and Campus HR to evaluate training progress, codebase familiarity, and attendance compliance.

3.4  Team Introduction

During the latter half of Week 1, interns are formally introduced to their assigned engineering cohort, technical mentor, and Delivery Unit Manager. This introduction bridges the transition from general HR induction to project-specific operations.

The Delivery Manager conducts a briefing outlining the business unit's domain focus (e.g. Banking & Financial Services, Retail, Healthcare, or High-Tech), current project portfolios, engineering methodologies, and expectations from the intern cohort.

Interns are also paired with a peer 'Buddy'—a young engineer who recently graduated from the internship program—who provides informal guidance on day-to-day campus life, team culture, tools, and best practices.

3.5  Initial Setup

Initial technical setup requires configuring corporate accounts, security agents, collaboration platforms, and administrative portals. Interns receive their official corporate email address (`firstname.lastname@zensar.com`) and enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) credentials.

Key configuration steps include: setting up Microsoft Authenticator multi-factor authentication (MFA); accessing the OneRPG portal (`https://rpgnet.sharepoint.com/sites/OneRPG`); configuring Microsoft Outlook and Teams; testing access to the Zensar Timesheet Portal (`https://timesheet.zensar.com`); and logging into Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion) for employee records.

Any setup impediments, such as locked domain accounts, VPN access failures, or missing software licenses, must be promptly escalated by raising a ticket on the IS Service Desk (`https://servicedesk.zensar.com`) under the TIMS category.

Onboarding Buddy and Mentor Engagement: Each engineering intern is paired with a designated onboarding buddy (a senior engineer or recent graduate trainee) to assist with practical campus navigation, development tool configurations, timesheet conventions, and team integration. Technical mentors provide daily coaching, conduct weekly code reviews, and monitor curriculum milestone completions.

Chapter 4: Intern Roles and Responsibilities

4.1  Role Expectations

As an engineering intern at Zensar, you occupy a dual role as an intensive technical learner and a contributing junior engineering professional. The organization expects interns to actively take ownership of their professional development while contributing meaningfully to team productivity.

Interns are expected to transition rapidly from passive instructional learning to active engineering exploration. This involves reading architectural specifications, asking informed questions during standups, investigating open-source libraries, and adopting industry-standard coding practices.

Interns are expected to operate with accountability—proactively communicating blockers, adhering to delivery deadlines, and seeking feedback on code quality and architectural decisions.

4.2  Responsibilities

The operational responsibilities of an intern span technical execution, team collaboration, continuous learning, and compliance. Interns must consistently demonstrate diligence and craftsmanship in every assigned task.

Technical responsibilities include: writing clean, modular, and maintainable code; adhering to language-specific style guides (e.g. Google Java Guide, PEP 8 Python); creating unit test suites with target code coverage (>80%); executing pull requests (PRs) via Git; and incorporating peer review feedback.

Operational responsibilities include: attending daily agile ceremonies (standups, sprint reviews, retrospectives); maintaining accurate task statuses in Jira or Azure DevOps; submitting weekly timesheets on Friday; and completing mandatory corporate learning modules on Pulse LMS.

4.3  Work Assignments

Work assignments evolve dynamically across the internship lifecycle. In the initial training phase, assignments consist of curated coding exercises, data structure implementations, RESTful API integrations, and frontend UI components.

As interns transition into project pods, work assignments transition into real user stories, such as developing microservice endpoints, creating responsive React web pages, writing automated integration tests, implementing data transformation pipelines, or building proof-of-concept AI agents.

All work assignments are managed through agile project management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or Git issues. Interns must update task progress daily, log estimated versus actual hours, and attach commit links to closed tickets.

4.4  Professional Expectations

Professionalism is the cornerstone of the Zensar workplace culture. Interns are expected to exhibit the highest standards of professional conduct, business etiquette, and emotional intelligence in all corporate interactions.

Key expectations include: practicing active listening; writing concise, grammatically sound emails and Teams messages; maintaining prompt calendar response etiquette (accepting/declining meetings promptly); dressing in smart business casuals; and respecting diverse viewpoints.

Confidentiality is paramount. Interns must never discuss client names, project architectures, or proprietary source code on personal social media platforms (LinkedIn, Twitter, GitHub), public discussion forums, or with external peers.

Chapter 5: Training and Learning Program

5.1  Training Syllabus

The Zensar Intern Training Syllabus is a rigorous, industry-aligned engineering curriculum designed to build enterprise-ready technologists. Curated by Zensar's Technical Learning & Development Academy in collaboration with Enterprise Architecture Practice heads, the curriculum spans core software engineering disciplines.

The syllabus covers four foundational modules: (1) Core Software Engineering Principles (Data Structures, Algorithms, Object-Oriented Design, Design Patterns, SOLID principles); (2) Modern Web & Backend Architecture (Java/Spring Boot, Python/FastAPI, Node.js, React, TypeScript); (3) Cloud & DevOps Foundations (AWS/Azure core services, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD with Jenkins/GitHub Actions); and (4) Enterprise Data & AI (Relational Databases, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Data Modeling, GenAI fundamentals, LLM prompting).

The syllabus also incorporates the RPG HR Academy and Wisdom Quest learning pathways, providing foundational modules on consulting acumen, customer empathy, and agile project delivery.

5.2  Training Schedule

The training schedule is structured into intensive full-day instructional and practical sessions running from Monday through Friday. A typical training day balances interactive instructor-led sessions with independent hands-on lab exercises and peer code reviews.

The standard daily schedule runs from 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM IST. Morning sessions (9:30 AM – 1:00 PM) are dedicated to theoretical concepts, architectural patterns, and live coding demonstrations by subject matter experts. Afternoon sessions (2:00 PM – 5:30 PM) focus on individual lab assignments, coding challenges, and pair programming.

The day concludes with a 1-hour wrap-up session (5:30 PM – 6:30 PM) where instructors review common debugging bottlenecks, answer questions, and publish the evening self-study resources.

5.3  Technical Training

Technical training at Zensar is delivered through a blended learning model combining live expert-led Masterclasses, interactive cloud sandbox labs, and self-paced digital courses on Pulse LMS. The emphasis is overwhelmingly placed on practical, experiential implementation.

Interns are assigned dedicated virtual sandbox environments with pre-configured developer toolchains, cloud accounts, and test datasets. This allows interns to experiment safely with distributed system deployments, database migrations, and microservice container orchestration without risking production environments.

Technical trainers are practicing Senior Technical Architects and Principal Engineers who bring immediate, practical project insights into the classroom.

5.4  Assignments

Assignments form the core operational benchmark of the training program. Interns are assigned daily coding exercises and weekly capstone mini-projects that reinforce concepts covered during lectures.

All assignments must be committed to Zensar's enterprise Bitbucket/GitLab repositories under designated assignment branches. Commits must follow standardized commit message conventions, include comprehensive unit test coverage (>80%), and pass automated static code analysis (SonarQube) gates.

Late submissions are penalized, and plagiarism—whether copying from external websites or peer repositories—is detected using automated code-similarity scanners and results in formal disciplinary escalation.

5.5  Assessments

Formal assessments occur at the conclusion of each technology module to measure competency and learning retention. Assessments comprise three evaluation modes: objective conceptual quizzes (MCQs), timed hands-on coding challenges (hackathon style), and technical viva voce interviews.

The minimum passing score for all module assessments is 75%. Interns who score between 60% and 74% are placed on supervised academic remediation and granted one re-assessment opportunity within 7 calendar days.

Consistent underperformance (scoring below 60% or failing re-assessments across multiple modules) triggers a formal performance review with the Campus HR Head and may jeopardize the intern's PPO conversion eligibility.

5.6  Learning Resources

Zensar provides interns with comprehensive access to premier enterprise learning libraries and internal knowledge repositories to support self-directed continuous upskilling.

Interns receive full enterprise access to Pulse LMS (Zensar's proprietary digital learning platform hosting curated learning journeys, video lectures, and lab guides). In addition, enterprise accounts are provisioned on external platforms such as Coursera Enterprise, Skillsoft Percipio, and O'Reilly Safari Books Online.

Interns can also access the Zensar Technical Knowledge Base on SharePoint, featuring whitepapers, reference architecture blueprints, and internal reusable software accelerators.

Chapter 6: Mentor and Reporting Structure

6.1  Mentor Responsibilities

Every intern at Zensar is formally paired with a designated Technical Mentor—an experienced Senior Software Engineer or Technical Lead within the assigned Delivery Unit. The mentor serves as a personal engineering coach, technical advisor, and professional role model throughout the internship tenure.

Key responsibilities of the mentor include: conducting daily or weekly 1-on-1 code reviews; explaining complex architectural patterns and domain business logic; providing guidance on debugging and performance optimization; facilitating connections with broader engineering teams; and offering constructive, candid feedback on technical growth.

Mentors also champion outstanding intern contributions for organizational recognition, including the prestigious Zensar Talent Recognition and Mentor/Mentee of the Year awards.

6.2  Reporting Manager

In addition to a technical mentor, each intern is assigned a formal Reporting Manager, typically a Delivery Manager, Project Manager, or Practice Lead. The Reporting Manager holds administrative and operational authority over the intern's engagement.

The Reporting Manager is responsible for: approving weekly timesheets on the Zensar Timesheet Portal; managing leave requests and attendance approvals; allocating project work assignments; conducting mid-term and final performance evaluations; and submitting the formal PPO conversion recommendation to Campus Talent Acquisition.

Interns should consult their Reporting Manager regarding any project escalations, changes in working arrangements, academic examination schedules, or contractual matters.

6.3  Guidance and Support

Zensar cultivates a nurturing, high-support ecosystem to help interns navigate the steep learning curve of enterprise software engineering. Support channels span peer, project, and institutional levels.

At the project level, interns participate in daily sprint ceremonies, pair programming sessions, and open technical clinics. At the institutional level, the Campus Talent Acquisition Team hosts monthly 'Connect with HR' check-ins to address any non-technical concerns or administrative bottlenecks.

For emotional well-being and personal support, interns have confidential access to the Zensarian Assistance Program (ZAP), providing free professional counseling services for stress management, career anxiety, and work-life balance.

6.4  Progress Updates

Maintaining continuous, transparent visibility into project and learning progress is a core professional discipline at Zensar. Interns participate in structured progress update cadences to align daily activities with business goals.

Daily updates are provided during the 15-minute Agile Standup, structured around the three standard questions: What did I complete yesterday? What am I working on today? What impediments or blockers am I facing?

Weekly written progress summaries are submitted to both the Technical Mentor and Reporting Manager every Friday afternoon, summarizing completed user stories, test coverage metrics, key learning takeaways, and planned goals for the upcoming week.

6.5  Escalation Procedures

When workplace challenges, technical bottlenecks, interpersonal conflicts, or administrative issues cannot be resolved through standard channels, interns should follow Zensar's formal hierarchical escalation procedure.

Level 1 Escalation: Discuss the issue directly with your assigned Technical Mentor or Peer Buddy for informal guidance and internal resolution.

Level 2 Escalation: If the issue remains unresolved or pertains to administrative, allocation, or timesheet matters, escalate formally to your Reporting Manager.

Level 3 Escalation: For sensitive personal matters, unresolved grievances, compensation disputes, or issues involving management, escalate to the Campus HR Program Lead or email `CampusHR@zensar.com`.

Chapter 7: Intern Attendance and Timesheets

7.1  Attendance Rules

Strict adherence to corporate attendance and working hour guidelines is mandatory for all Zensar interns. Interns are contracted to work standard full-time corporate hours: 9 hours per day (inclusive of a 1-hour lunch and refreshment breaks), amounting to 45 hours per week, Monday through Friday.

For physical campus reporting, attendance is recorded electronically via RFID smart card access swipes at turnstiles and biometric access readers. Interns must record both arrival and departure swipes daily. Missing swipes result in automated system marking of absence.

For approved remote or hybrid work days, attendance is tracked via VPN session logging and Microsoft Teams active availability. Interns must maintain an overall attendance record of at least 90% across the internship tenure to remain eligible for stipend disbursement and PPO conversion.

ZenTimesheet System Walkthrough: Intern daily effort and project hours are tracked through the official ZenTimesheet platform (https://timesheet.zensar.com/login). Interns sign in using Single Sign-On (SSO) credentials. The interface displays a 7-day weekly grid (Monday through Sunday) reflecting allocated project codes, training assignments, and approved leaves automatically synchronized from Zenith.

Training & Foundation WBS Coding: Unlike billable associates who log time to client project codes, interns must log effort under their designated Training / Foundation WBS Code (e.g., Campus Foundation Program WBS). Standard working hours must be logged as 8 hours per day (40 hours per week). Any approved leaves (e.g., examination or casual leave) logged in Zenith automatically reflect on the timesheet grid and must not be double-booked as training hours.

7.2  Timesheet Submission

All interns must log their daily working hours on the official Zensar Timesheet Portal (`https://timesheet.zensar.com/login` or via OneRPG SSO under `My Applications > Timesheet`). Accurate timesheet submission is the primary statutory record governing stipend disbursement and project accounting.

Interns must log exactly 9 hours per working day against the designated Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) Internal Order Code provided by their manager (e.g. Intern Training Internal Order or Specific Project Task Code). Timesheets must be submitted on a weekly cycle, no later than Friday 6:00 PM IST.

Zensar enforces a strict 10-working-day lookback window policy. Timesheets not submitted within this window are locked by the enterprise ERP, requiring special managerial escalation and HR approval to unlock, which causes delays in monthly stipend processing.

Timesheet Submission and Approval Rhythm: (1) Save Draft: Interns can enter daily hours and click 'Save Draft' at the close of each day; (2) Weekly Submission Cutoff: Complete weekly timesheets must be formally submitted by clicking 'Submit' every Friday by 18:00 IST; (3) Mentor Approval Deadline: Technical mentors / reporting managers review and approve timesheets by Monday 12:00 IST; (4) Rejection Workflow: If a timesheet is rejected, the intern receives an automated email notification citing the manager's comments. The intern must immediately navigate to https://timesheet.zensar.com/login, revise the flagged entries, and resubmit for approval; and (5) 10-Day Lockout: Timesheets older than 10 calendar days are automatically frozen and cannot be modified without exceptional approval from Campus Delivery Leadership.

7.3  Timesheet Approval

Once an intern submits their weekly timesheet, it routes electronically to their assigned Reporting Manager for review and approval. Managers verify that the logged hours, task descriptions, and project codes align with assigned work.

Managerial approvals must be executed by Monday 12:00 PM IST following the submission week. If an entry contains errors (such as incorrect project code or mismatched hours), the manager rejects the timesheet with explanatory notes.

Interns receive an automated email notification when a timesheet is rejected. The intern must immediately correct the highlighted discrepancy and resubmit the timesheet before Tuesday 5:00 PM IST to avoid payroll processing disruption.

7.4  Attendance Corrections

In instances where an intern forgets to swipe their RFID badge, experiences a card reader malfunction, or performs official off-site activities, an attendance correction request must be initiated.

Attendance regularizations must be submitted via ZenFusion or the Attendance Management module on OneRPG within 3 business days of the incident. The intern must select the date, specify the actual arrival and departure times, and provide a valid operational justification.

The regularization routes to the Reporting Manager for electronic sign-off. Frequent attendance regularizations (more than 3 per month) are flagged by HR Operations for supervisory review.

Chapter 8: Project Allocation and Work Management

8.1  Project Allocation

Upon successful completion of the foundational training phase and clearing benchmark assessments, interns are allocated to active engineering projects within Zensar's Delivery Units. Project allocation is governed by enterprise business demand, client engagement requirements, and the intern's demonstrated technical competencies.

Delivery Units span major industry verticals, including Financial Services & Insurance, Retail & Consumer Goods, Healthcare & Life Sciences, and High-Tech & Manufacturing. Interns may be assigned to client delivery squads, internal enterprise platform modernization teams, or the Zensar Innovation Lab.

The allocation process is formalized through a project onboarding briefing where the Delivery Manager outlines the client context, architectural landscape, project timeline, and specific intern deliverables.

8.2  Task Assignment

Tasks within project teams are assigned through agile sprint planning sessions. Interns are assigned granular user stories, engineering tasks, or bug fixes from the sprint backlog.

Each task assignment includes defined acceptance criteria, definition of done (DoD), architectural constraints, and estimated story points or hours. Interns must review requirements thoroughly before committing to deliver within the sprint.

Tasks are tracked via enterprise tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps Boards, or Rally. Interns are responsible for updating ticket statuses (e.g. In Progress, In Code Review, Testing, Done) in real time.

8.3  Deliverables

Intern deliverables reflect enterprise engineering quality standards. Depending on the assigned project, deliverables typically include functional microservices, responsive web user interfaces, automated test suites, database migration scripts, or technical architecture documentation.

All code deliverables must strictly conform to Zensar's Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) protocols. Code must be free from known vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10), pass SonarQube static code analysis with zero high-severity issues, and include clean inline documentation.

Non-code deliverables include API specifications (Swagger/OpenAPI), architecture diagrams, user guides, and deployment runbooks.

8.4  Progress Reporting

Structured progress reporting ensures that project managers and mentors maintain accurate visibility into sprint velocity and potential project risks. Interns report progress through three standard channels.

First, interns participate in the Daily Agile Standup, providing a crisp 2-minute overview of completed tasks, ongoing work, and impediments. Second, interns maintain real-time task progress and burn-down charts on Jira/Azure DevOps.

Third, interns submit a comprehensive Weekly Status Report (WSR) to their mentor and manager every Friday, detailing completed tasks, code review links, upcoming sprint commitments, and any dependencies requiring management intervention.

8.5  Project Reviews

Project work is subject to formal periodic reviews to validate code craftsmanship, architectural adherence, and delivery timeliness. Reviews occur at three distinct levels: peer code reviews, sprint demos, and milestone performance reviews.

Peer Code Reviews are conducted on every pull request (PR). A PR cannot be merged into the main development branch without receiving formal approval from at least one senior engineer and the Technical Mentor.

Sprint Demos occur at the conclusion of each 2-week sprint, where interns demonstrate working software features to the entire cross-functional team, product owners, and client stakeholders.

Chapter 9: Intern Leave and Holidays

9.1  Applicable Leave Rules

Because an internship is an intensive, time-bound training program, standard full-time employee paid leave entitlements (such as Annual Privileged Leave accruals) do not apply to interns in the same manner. However, Zensar recognizes that personal emergencies, health issues, and mandatory academic requirements require structured leave provisions.

Interns are typically permitted up to 1 day of casual/sick leave per completed month of internship for genuine medical illness or unforeseen personal emergencies. Unused intern leaves lapse at the end of the internship tenure and cannot be encashed or carried forward into full-time employment.

For academic commitments, such as mandatory university semester examinations or final project vivas, interns may be granted Academic Leave upon submitting official examination schedules endorsed by their college Principal or Registrar.

9.2  Leave Request Process

All leave requests must be formally submitted and approved in advance through the designated HR portal—Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion) under `OneRPG > My Applications > ZenFusion > Me > Time and Absences`.

For planned leaves (including academic examinations), requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance, accompanied by official supporting documents (such as university exam notices). This enables managers to adjust sprint task distributions.

In cases of sudden illness or emergency, the intern must notify their Technical Mentor and Reporting Manager via email or Microsoft Teams by 9:30 AM IST on the day of absence, and submit the formal system leave application immediately upon resuming work.

9.3  Approval Process

Once a leave application is lodged in ZenFusion, it routes electronically to the intern's Reporting Manager for assessment and approval. The manager evaluates the request against current sprint commitments, training milestones, and remaining leave balances.

Approved leaves are reflected automatically in the enterprise attendance system. If a leave request is rejected due to critical delivery deadlines or insufficient justification, the manager provides written remarks, and the intern must report to work as scheduled.

Proceeding on leave without obtaining formal system approval constitutes unauthorized absence (Leave Without Pay) and will result in stipend deductions and disciplinary review.

9.4  Holiday Guidelines

Chapter 10: Intern Performance and Evaluation

10.1  Performance Expectations

Performance expectations for Zensar interns are designed to foster technical excellence, engineering discipline, and cultural integration. Interns are evaluated holistically across both technical deliverables and behavioral competencies.

Interns are expected to consistently deliver functional, testable code on schedule; demonstrate intellectual agility by rapidly absorbing feedback; adhere rigorously to agile development processes; and contribute constructively to team discussions.

High performance also requires active demonstration of the RPG Group 'Values in Motion'—operating with high velocity, maintaining ethical transparency, and displaying a genuine passion to outperform.

10.2  Assessment Criteria

Zensar employs a structured 5-Parameter Evaluation Framework to ensure fair, objective, and transparent performance appraisals across all intern cohorts. Each parameter carries a specific percentage weight contributing to the cumulative score.

The evaluation criteria comprise: (1) Technical Competence & Code Quality (30%); (2) Problem Solving & Learning Agility (25%); (3) Timeliness & Delivery Execution (15%); (4) Communication & Team Collaboration (15%); and (5) Values in Motion & Professional Conduct (15%).

Cumulative scores are benchmarked against standardized performance ratings: Exceeds Expectations (>=85%), Meets Expectations (75%–84%), Needs Improvement (60%–74%), and Unsatisfactory (<60%).

10.3  Feedback Process

Continuous feedback is fundamental to the Zensar learning philosophy. Interns receive ongoing informal and formal feedback throughout their tenure to ensure continuous improvement and avoid year-end surprises.

Informal feedback is provided during daily standups, weekly 1-on-1 mentor syncs, and pull request reviews. Mentors provide immediate, actionable feedback on code structure, algorithm efficiency, and testing methodology.

Formal feedback sessions occur during Mid-Term and Final evaluations. In these structured reviews, the manager and mentor walk the intern through their parameter scores, highlight notable strengths, identify specific technical development areas, and establish concrete action plans.

10.4  Evaluation Schedule

The performance evaluation schedule is structured across three formal milestone checkpoints over the course of the internship tenure.

Checkpoint 1: 30-Day Foundation Review. Focuses on onboarding completion, baseline training quiz scores, and adaptation to corporate tooling.

Checkpoint 2: Mid-Term Evaluation (Day 90 for 6-month cohorts). A comprehensive appraisal assessing module sprint assessments, project contributions, and agile participation. Interns with scores below 75% are placed on targeted mentoring.

Checkpoint 3: Final Capstone Defense & PPO Review (Day 160–175). Final evaluation assessing the capstone project defense, end-to-end code craftsmanship, cumulative attendance, and overall business value.

10.5  Progress Tracking

Intern performance data is systematically logged and tracked in Zensar's enterprise talent systems. The Campus Talent Acquisition Team and Delivery Unit leadership maintain consolidated dashboards monitoring attendance, assessment scores, timesheet compliance, and mentor evaluations.

Interns can monitor their training progress and quiz scores directly through Pulse LMS under their personalized learner profile dashboard.

High-performing interns who consistently achieve scores above 85% and demonstrate outstanding leadership in collaborative hackathons are nominated for special recognitions, including the Zensar Spotlight and RPG Group young innovator awards.

The stipend is an all-inclusive consolidated amount and does not carry separate allowances (such as HRA, Medical, or Special Allowance).

Because interns are engaged under a temporary training contract rather than as permanent employees, standard statutory provident fund (PF), employee state insurance (ESI), and gratuity deductions are not applicable to stipend disbursements.

Chapter 13: Internship Completion

13.1  Final Evaluation

The culmination of the Zensar Internship Program involves a comprehensive Final Evaluation and Capstone Defense conducted two weeks prior to the internship completion date. This evaluation serves as the definitive assessment governing internship completion grading and full-time PPO conversion recommendations.

The evaluation panel consists of the Delivery Unit Head, Senior Technical Architect, Practice Lead, and Campus Talent Acquisition Partner. Interns deliver a formal 30-minute presentation and live architectural demonstration of their capstone engineering project.

The panel evaluates the intern across five core dimensions: architectural design and code craftsmanship; system robustness and test coverage; business value delivered; mastery of agile processes; and ability to defend technical decisions during the live technical Q&A session.

13.2  Project Handover

Prior to exiting the organization, interns must execute a structured, comprehensive project handover to ensure uninterrupted continuity of engineering deliverables.

Handover requirements include: committing and pushing all final source code to approved Bitbucket/GitLab branches; ensuring all open pull requests are merged or reassigned; writing detailed technical handover documentation (including system architecture overview, API endpoint catalogs, database schemas, and deployment instructions); and uploading documentation to the project's Confluence/SharePoint workspace.

The Technical Mentor must conduct a formal walkthrough of the handover documentation and execute the Project Handover Sign-Off Form confirming that all assets, code, and documentation are properly transitioned.

13.3  Feedback

The completion process incorporates a 360-degree feedback mechanism. In addition to receiving their final evaluation scores, interns are provided with a dedicated platform to share candid, constructive feedback regarding their internship experience.

Interns complete the anonymous End-of-Internship Experience Survey on Pulse LMS. The survey evaluates key program dimensions: quality of training syllabus; effectiveness of technical mentors; relevance of project assignments; clarity of management communication; and overall campus culture.

Feedback insights are analyzed by the Campus Talent Acquisition Team and executive leadership to drive continuous curriculum enhancement, mentor training, and operational improvements for future cohorts.

Administrative closure requires the completion of standardized offboarding formalities via the Zensar eForms clearance portal at least 5 business days prior to the last working day.

The clearance workflow requires electronic departmental approvals: (1) Project / Practice Clearance: confirmation of code handover and timesheet sign-offs; (2) IT Asset Clearance: physical return and inspection of laptop, power brick, security tokens, and peripherals to the TIMS IT counter; (3) Security & Administration: surrender of RFID smart badge and clearance of campus dues; and (4) Finance & Payroll: reconciliation of stipend, expense claims, and tax documentation.

14.1  Intern Onboarding FAQs

This section addresses the most common questions raised by incoming interns regarding Day 1 reporting, document verification, campus logistics, and initial onboarding.

Q1: What should I do if my university exam dates clash with my Day 1 joining date?
A: Immediately inform your Campus Talent Acquisition Coordinator and email `CampusHR@zensar.com` with a copy of your official university examination notification. Joining dates can typically be adjusted to the subsequent onboarding batch with prior approval.

A: Business formal or smart casual attire is required from Monday through Thursday (collared shirts, formal trousers, business dresses). Friday is smart casual (clean jeans and polo t-shirts permitted). Round-neck t-shirts, athletic wear, and open slippers are strictly prohibited.

14.2  Academic & Training FAQs

This section provides clarity on common academic and technical training queries encountered during the internship program.

Q1: What happens if I fail a module benchmark assessment?
A: If you score between 60% and 74%, you are provided with 7 days of supervised academic remediation followed by one re-assessment opportunity. Scoring below 60% triggers a formal review with your Technical Mentor and Campus HR.

Q2: How do I apply for leave for college semester examinations?
A: Submit an Academic Leave request on ZenFusion at least 5 business days in advance, attaching the official examination timetable approved by your college Principal or Head of Department. Also inform your Reporting Manager so sprint task allocations can be adjusted.

A: Track assignments are based on organizational client demand, project pipeline requirements, and your performance in the initial engineering aptitude evaluation.

Q1: When will my monthly stipend be credited?
A: The monthly stipend is credited on the last working day of each calendar month, provided all weekly timesheets are approved and bank details were verified on ZenFusion before the 15th.

Q2: Is income tax deducted from my stipend?
A: Stipends are subject to Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) under applicable Indian Income Tax Act regulations (such as Section 194J) if the annual payout exceeds statutory thresholds. TDS certificates (Form 16A) are issued quarterly.

A: Review the rejection remarks in the Timesheet Portal, rectify the specific issue (such as incorrect project code or mismatched hours), and resubmit the timesheet before Tuesday 5:00 PM IST.
